history.dynasty: None documented (19th-century origins; no dynasty attribution found in sources)
history.period: 19th century (about 150 years old per local accounts)
history.summary: The Shri Rupabhavani Temple at Bhavani Peth, Solapur, is a Shakti shrine dedicated to Bhavani Devi, worshipped as a form of Tulja Bhavani, the kuladevi (family goddess) of Maharashtra. Local accounts date the temple to about 150 years ago, i.e. the 19th century, and describe it as a stone temple with beautiful engravings. Folklore holds that Bhavani Devi protects the town of Solapur, and the temple has served as a Hindu religious hub of the city for over a century. It stands at Bhavani Peth (Solapur 413002, about 2-4 km from the city centre and roughly 2 km from the ST bus stand) and draws large crowds during Navratri. Detailed historical records of its construction, patronage, and deity installation were not found in accessible sources (verify); its legends link it to the Tulja Bhavani tradition rather than to the neighbouring Siddheshwar temple complex.

name: Shri Rupabhavani Temple
town_description: Solapur, in south-west Maharashtra on the Maharashtra-Karnataka border, is a major textile and powerloom city known as Siddheshwar Nagari after the 16th-century Siddheshwar (Shiva) temple at its heart. Its landmarks include the Siddheshwar lake and temple, the 14th-century Bhui-kot fort in the city centre, and the Markandeya temple; Solapur lies on the Mumbai-Hyderabad rail corridor and attracts lakhs of pilgrims yearly.

travel.airport: Pune International Airport (approx. 250 km; roughly a 4-hour drive - the nearest major international airport with wide connectivity). Solapur city also has a small airport with limited commercial flights (verify current schedules).
travel.railway: Solapur Junction Railway Station (on the Mumbai-Hyderabad main line, approx. 400 km from Mumbai; the temple at Bhavani Peth is about 2-4 km from the city centre, reached by auto-rickshaw, taxi or city bus).
travel.road: The temple is at Bhavani Peth, Solapur (PIN 413002), about 2 km from the ST bus stand. Solapur is well connected by state transport (MSRTC) and private buses to Pune, Mumbai, Hyderabad and Kolhapur.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for pleasant weather. Navratri (September-October) is the most vibrant time to visit but draws heavy crowds; weekday mornings are best for a peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily approx. 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM (verify - Google business listings report 6 AM-9 PM; one temple listing reports 6:30 AM-7:30 PM and another 7:30 AM-1:00 PM and 4:30-8:30 PM). No entry fee reported; dress modestly and remove footwear before entering.
